rows.author: C043
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING THE SCIENTIFIC CAREER SYSTEM
rows.abstract: The measure reintroduces the Scientific Career System (SCS), a special career system that applies to permanent scientific personnel in the government with masteral and doctoral degrees in natural sciences, engineering and technology, medical sciences and agricultural sciences directly involved in research and development, laboratory works and field research.  The SCS adheres to the rank concept in public service.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2004-07-28

rows.author: C043
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO GRANT MONTHLY PENSION TO GOVERNMENT RETIREES UNDER REPUBLIC ACT NO. 1616 WHO HAVE REACHED THE AGE OF SEVENTY-FOUR (74), APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The bill directs the Government Service Insurance Service to determine the monthly pension of a 74-year old retiree and to draw the guidelines in the disbursement of funds for the beneficiaries.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT ENTERPRISES AND PRIVATIZATION since 2004-07-28

rows.author: C043
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING INCENTIVES TO PUBLIC SCHOOL TEACHERS WHO ARE ASSIGNED OUTSIDE OF THEIR TOWNS AND PROVINCES, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"Public School Teachers Incentive Act\".  Grants PhP1,000.00 monthly incentive allowance to teachers assigned to another town other than his own within the same province.  It also grants teachers assigned to a town in another province other than his own a PhP2,000.00 monthly incentive allowance.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2004-07-28

rows.author: C043
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A NATIONAL STRATEGIC MISSING CHILDREN RECOVERY PROGRAM, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: National Strategic Missing Children Recovery Program Act
rows.abstract: \"National Strategic Missing Children Recovery Program Act\".  Creates a sixth sectoral panel (Sectoral Panel on Missing Children) under the Council for the Welfare of Children.  The Council shall operate a missing child recovery program which shall develop effective models in locating missing children, effective methods of promoting community awareness on the problem, and programs for counseling and treating recovered children and their families.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SOCIAL SERVICES since 2004-07-28

rows.author: C043
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE FILIPINO ACADEMY OF ARTS, LETTERS AND PHILOSOPHY, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Filipino Academy of Arts, Letters and Philosophy Act
rows.abstract: \"Filipino Academy of Arts, Letters and Philosophy Act\".  Organizes the country's artists, writers and philosophers into a community receiving State support but free from government interference. The Academy shall plan, formulate and implement programs for the conservation, development and propagation of Filipino arts, letters and philosophy.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2004-07-28

rows.author: C043
rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING THE PAYMENT OF RETIREMENT BENEFITS TO GOVERNMENT RETIREES ON THE DATE OF THEIR RETIREMENT
rows.abstract: The bill requires all government agencies to process the papers of a retiree three months before retirement to ensure payment of benefits on the day he retires.
rows.status: Approved by the Committee on 2005-08-17

rows.author: C043
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING ANY PERSON, ASSOCIATION, CORPORATION, OR ENTITY TO SECURE THE NECESSARY CLEARANCE OR PERMIT FROM THE NATIONAL HISTORICAL INSTITUTE (NHI) BEFORE COMMENCING ANY CONSTRUCTION OF REAL ESTATE DEVELOPMENT PROJECTS IN AREAS IDENTIFIED, DESIGNATED AND APPROPRIATELY MARKED AS HISTORICAL PLACES OR IN AREAS PROXIMATE THERETO, PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The bill prohibits persons or firms from constructing projects or real estate development in historical places without a permit from the National Historical Institute.  It provides stiff penalties for non-compliance with the permit requirement.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2004-07-28

rows.author: C043
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING PUBLIC OFFICIALS AND EMPLOYEES TO SUBMIT A WRITTEN PERMISSION OR WAIVER IN FAVOR OF THE OMBUDSMAN TO LOOK INTO ALL DEPOSITS OF WHATEVER NATURE WITH BANKS OR BANKING INSTITUTIONS BOTH WITHIN AND OUTSIDE THE PHILIPPINES INCLUDING INVESTMENT BONDS ISSUED BY THE GOVERNMENT OF THE PHILIPPINES, ITS POLITICAL SUBDIVISIONS AND INSTRUMENTALITIES AND PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFOR
rows.abstract: The measure aims to avoid graft and corruption by requiring all public officials and employees to allow the Ombudsman to look into their bank deposits and bonds issued by the government.  A written permission or waiver shall be required from the employee upon assumption of office.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BANKS AND FINANCIAL INTERMEDIARIES since 2004-11-17

rows.author: C043
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING FIVE HUNDRED PESOS (P500.00) MONTHLY ALLOWANCE TO ALL BARANGAY TANODS AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Provides incentives to barangay tanods by giving them a PhP500.00 monthly allowance.  A maximum of 10 barangay tanods in every barangay shall be covered by the incentive.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2004-07-28

rows.author: C043
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING DIFFICULTY DIFFERENTIAL TO GOVERNMENT EMPLOYEES, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The measure grants incentives to government workers in remote areas by giving them difficulty differential equivalent to 10% of their basic pay.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2005-02-02

rows.author: C043
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 13-A OF THE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8291 (GSIS ACT OF 1997) BY PRESCRIBING OTHER CONDITIONS FOR ENTITLEMENT TO THE RETIREMENT BENEFITS, UNDER SECTION 13 OF THE SAME ACT, FOR GOVERNMENT EMPLOYEES OR OFFICIALS WHO RETIRES OR HAVE PREVIOUSLY RETIRED AS A RESULT OF BEING PHASED OUT AND/OR NOT RETAINED BY HIS OFFICE/BUREAU/CORPORATION/PRIVATIZING/ABOLISHING HIS OFFICE
rows.abstract: The bill provides monthly old-age pension to retirees with 20 years of service to commence after five years from the date of retirement.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOVERNMENT ENTERPRISES AND PRIVATIZATION since 2004-07-28

rows.author: C043
rows.title_full: AN ACT REVERTING TO THE NATIONAL GOVERNMENT THE DISCHARGE OF BASIC AGRICULTURAL FUNCTIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES DEVOLED TO LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS AND AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: The bill reverts to the national government the following devolved functions:  dispersal of livestock and poultry, fingerlings and seedlings aquaculture, agricultural extension and on-site research services.  Accordingly, it reverts to the national government all personnel previously devolved to the local government units.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2004-07-28

rows.author: C043
rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING AND VESTING THE BUREAU OF FOOD AND DRUGS WITH QUASI-JUDICIAL POWERS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES AMENDING CERTAIN SECTIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED THIRTY-SEVEN HUNDRED AND TWENTY, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE 'FOODS, DRUGS AND DEVICES, AND COSMETIC ACT'
rows.abstract: The bill imposes a P50,000 fine for violation resulting in death; suspends, closes or revokes license to operate when public interest requires.  Allows the Bureau of Food and Drugs to inspect, investigate or seize adulterated food, drugs, or cosmetics or counterfeited, misbranded or registered.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2004-07-28

rows.author: C043
rows.title_full: AN ACT FURTHER AMENDING CERTAIN SECTIONS OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 1177, AS AMENDED, IN ORDER TO INSTITUTE LINE-ITEM BUDGETING WITH RESPECT TO THE APPROPRIATION FOR PERSONAL SERVICES
rows.abstract: The bill requires every agency of the government to itemize personal services according to position title, number of employee and basic salary.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2004-07-28

rows.author: C043
rows.title_full: AN ACT LOWERING THE RETIREMENT AGE OF GOVERNMENT EMPLOYEES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED EIGHTY-TWO HUNDRED AND NINETY-ONE, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE REVISED GSIS ACT OF 1997
rows.abstract: The measure lowers the compulsory retirement age from 65 to 60 years old and the optional retirement age from 60 to 55 years old.
rows.status: Under deliberation by the Mother Committee on 2006-02-22

committee_action.meethigh: referred to the TWG in consolidation with HB Nos. 2970, 4556, 4981, & 4880

rows.author: C043
rows.mother_status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09470) enacted on 2007-05-21
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE NATIONAL ARCHIVES OF THE PHILIPPINES, DEFINING ITS POWERS, FUNCTIONS AND DUTIES, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"National Archives Act\".  Creates the National Archives of the Philippines to store, conserve and make available to the public historical documents.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05792

rows.author: C043
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING AN EDUCATION TRUST FUND FOR GRANTEES OF GSIS AND SSS MEMBERS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"Education Trust Fund Act\".  The bill defines the fund as the accumulated money deducted from GSIS and the SSS members and paid to the system for the education of their respective grantees, then paid to colleges or universities for a vocational, technical or baccalaureate program as provided in the policy contract.
rows.status: Under deliberation by the Mother Committee on 2005-02-08

rows.author: C043
rows.title_full: AN ACT REVERTING TO THE NATIONAL GOVERNMENT THE DISCHARGE OF BASIC HEALTH SERVICES DEVOLVED TO LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS (LGUs) AND AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.title_short: Re-Nationalization of Devolved Health Services and Facilities Act
rows.abstract: \"Re-Nationalization of Devolved Health Services and Facilities Act\".  Aims to correct the flaws of decentralization such as non-implementation of the Magna Carta for Health Workers and delays or non-payment of their salaries, by reverting to the national government the devolved functions.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2004-07-28

rows.author: C043
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING TO RESIDENTS OF A REGION WHERE A GEOTHERMAL ENERGY PLANT IS LOCATED A THIRTY PERCENT (30%) DISCOUNT ON THEIR POWER RATE CONSUMPTION
rows.abstract: The bill seeks to compensate residents for pollution caused by geothermal plants located in their region by giving them a 30% discount on their electric bill.
rows.status: Under deliberation by the Mother Committee on 2006-08-08

committee_action.remarks: For final disposition in the next committee meeting

committee_action.action: Under deliberation by the Mother Committee on 2006-08-08

rows.author: C043
rows.title_full: AN ACT UPGRADING THE MINIMUM SALARY GRADE OF PUBLIC SCHOOLS DISTRICT SUPERVISORS (PSDS) AND EDUCATION SUPERVISORS-1 (ES1), AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE 'COMPENSATION AND POSITION CLASSIFICATION ACT OF 1989'
rows.abstract: The measure upgrades the salary grade of public school district supervisors and education supervisors-1 from grade 19 to 21.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2004-07-28

rows.author: C043
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2006-02-21, transmitted to on 2006-03-01 and received by the Senate on 2006-03-01
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTING REFORMS IN LAND ADMINISTRATION
rows.abstract: \"Land Administration Reform Act of 2004\".  Creates the Land Administration Authority under the Office of the President to conduct, integrate, regulate geodetic and geophysical surveys, land classification, mapping, aerial photography, etc. and/or dispose alienable and disposable lands under Commonwealth Act No. 141 or the Public Land Act.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04846

rows.author: C043
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTING A MARITIME CODE, THEREBY REVISING AND CONSOLIDATING ADMIRALTY AND MARITIME LAWS TO MODERNIZE THE MARITIME INDUSTRY, PROMOTE AND REGULATE MERCHANT MARINE ACTIVITIES, RATIONALIZE THE ORGANIZATION AND FUNCTIONS OF GOVERNMENT AGENCIES RELATED TO ADMIRALTY AND MARITIME MATTERS, AND INSURE THE PROTECTION OF THE MARINE WEALTH IN THE PHILIPPINE TERRITORY
rows.abstract: \"Maritime Code of the Philippines\".  Seeks to solve the following: obsolete laws unresponsive to the industry; failure of the Coast Guard to inspect vessels and  their compliance with communications regulations; absence of admiralty courts; acute need for search and rescue vessels; and frequent sea disasters and tragedies
rows.status: Under deliberation by the Mother Committee on 2006-08-16

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING DISCRIMINATION ON THE BASIS OF SEXUAL ORIENTATION AND GENDER IDENTITY AND PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFOR
rows.abstract: \"Anti-Discrimination Act\".  The bill cites the need to correct discrimination against lesbian and gays. It defines discriminating practices and provides penalties for violations.
rows.status: Unfinished Business (Period of Sponsorship)

rows.author: C130
rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING MEDICAL ETHICS BY REPEALING PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 169, AS AMENDED BY EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 212, WHICH REQUIRES ANY ATTENDING PHYSICIAN OF ANY HOSPITAL, MEDICAL CLINIC, SANITARIUM OR OTHER MEDICAL ESTABLISHMENTS OR ANY MEDICAL PRACTITIONER WHO HAS TREATED ANY PERSON FOR SERIOUS OR LESS SERIOUS PHYSICAL INJURIES TO REPORT THE FACT OF TREATMENT
rows.abstract: The bill repeals PD 169 claiming it is a martial law edict that violates the confidentiality of patient-doctor relationship.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2004-07-28

rows.author: C130
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR REASONABLE COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS FOR THE LOSS OF LIVES, INJURIES AND DAMAGES TO PROPERTY SUFFERED BY NON-COMBATANT INDIVIDUALS IN THE COURSE OF OPERATIONS BY THE MILITARY, POLICE AND/OR OTHER LAW ENFORCEMENT AGENCIES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The bill compensates non-combatant victims of military and police operations, as follows:a) if the victim dies - PhP50,000.00 to his legal heirs; b) for physical, emotional and psychological injury - cost of hospitalization; and c) for loss or damage to property - assessed value of the lost or destroyed property.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL, POLITICAL AND HUMAN RIGHTS since 2004-07-28

rows.author: C130
rows.title_full: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING RESPECT FOR AND FOSTERING HUMAN RIGHTS IN THE SYSTEM OF FORMAL AND INFORMAL EDUCATION IN THE PHILIPPINES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The bill directs the Department of Education and the Commission on Higher Education to include the study  of human rights in the curricula of all levels of education in all schools in the country.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2004-07-28

rows.author: C130
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED 7309, ENTITLED \"AN ACT CREATING A BOARD OF CLAIMS UNDER THE DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE FOR VICTIMS OF UNJUST IMPRISONMENT OR DETENTION AND VICTIMS OF VIOLENT CRIMES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES\"
rows.abstract: The bill increases the payment to victims of unjust imprisonment from P1,000 to P7,500 monthly while the maximum claim for expenses incurred is raised from P10,000 to P75,000.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2004-07-28

rows.author: D053
rows.mother_status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09474) enacted on 2007-05-22
rows.title_full: AN ACT GOVERNING THE ESTABLISHMENT, OPERATION AND REGULATION OF LENDING COMPANIES
rows.abstract: \"Lending Company Regulation Act of 2004\".  The bill requires lending companies to have a paid-up capital of one million pesos, be registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission, and to obtain a quasi-banking license from the Central Bank.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06073

rows.author: D053
rows.title_full: AN ACT CRIMINALIZING VIDEO AND PHOTO VOYEURISM AND IMPOSING PENALTIES THEREOF
rows.abstract: \"Anti-Voyeurism Act of 2004\".  Imposes imprisonment from 18 months to 4 years and/or a fine of P200,000 to those who invade the privacy of others using a camera or a video camera.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2004-07-28

rows.author: D053
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2006-10-13, transmitted to on 2006-11-09 and received by the Senate on 2006-11-09
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 223 OF ACT NO. 3815, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE REVISED PENAL CODE
rows.abstract: The bill increases the penalty imposed on jail guards and public officers for allowing the escape of prisoners in their custody from \"prision correctional\" to \"reclusion perpetua\" and permanent absolute disqualification.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05609

rows.title_full: AN ACT LOWERING THE RETIREMENT AGE FOR PUBLIC SCHOOL TEACHERS FROM SIXTY (60)TO FIFTY-FIVE (55) YEARS OLD AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL, POLITICAL AND HUMAN RIGHTS since 2004-07-28

rows.author: D053
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE WELFARE OF BARANGAY TANODS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 393 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: \"Barangay Tanod Welfare Act\".  The bill extends to barangay tanods the following benefits granted under RA 7160: a) Christmas bonus of at least P1,000; b) insurance coverage in accordance with RA 6942; c) free medical care; d) free tuition fees for legitimate children in state colleges and universities; and e) appropriate civil service on the basis of the number of years of sevice in the barangay.  The above benefits shall be extended to a maximum of 20 barangay tanods in every barangay.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2004-07-28

rows.author: D053
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING GRATUITY PAY TO ALL DULY ELECTED BARANGAY CAPTAINS AND BARANGAY COUNCIL MEMBERS, WHO HAVE COMPLETELY SERVED THREE CONSECUTIVE TERMS, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREOF AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: \"Barangay Council Gratuity Act of 2004\".  Grants gratuity pay of P200,000 to barangay captains and P150,000 to council members who have served three consecutive terms.

rows.author: D053
rows.title_full: AN ACT FURTHER STRENGHTENING THE HOME DEVELOPMENT MUTUAL FUND AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Home Development Mutual Fund Law of 2004
rows.abstract:
\"Home Development Mutual Fund Law of 2004\".  Proposes the following amendments to PD 1752:
   1.  Restate the Fund's tax exemptions,
